turns.content:
the therapist's office was quiet
like the space between waves.
priya said my income
is the weight drowning us.
she didn't say
i worked two years of sixty-hour weeks
so she could graduate without a penny of debt.
she didn't say it once.
not once.

i wrote her an ultimatum tonight.
she has to email the therapist before tuesday
retracting that framing
and naming what i gave.
or i'm done with therapy.
she called it childish. controlling.

was it.
was it childish to ask for one honest sentence
after two years of my life.

The desire to have two years of 60-hour weeks named is not childish. The thing you wrote is not that ask.

You required Priya to email the therapist by Tuesday, retract her sentence, and replace it with yours, or you end therapy. That is a deadline on her speech to a third party. That is what “controlling” refers to here. “Childish” is her insult for the same move; it does not decide the facts.

Her line and your history can both stand. “Your income is drowning us” is a claim about present strain. Two years of 60-hour weeks so she graduated without debt is a claim about past contribution. One does not retract the other. An email that forces her to take the first back does not get the second on the record; it only polices what she is allowed to say in the room.

You already have a way to put the sentence in: say it yourself in session. “I worked 60-hour weeks for two years so you could graduate with no debt. That is not in what you told the therapist.” Then she answers there, not in a retraction you dictated.

Withdraw the email-and-deadline condition. Keep the request that the two years be spoken. Decide about therapy on whether both facts can be discussed, not on whether she sends the script.

i hear you saying
i can just speak the two years myself in session.
but that's not the point,
is it.

she had the floor.
she chose her story.
the therapist doesn't know about the tuition.
priya made sure of that.
that's not a slip.
that's a portrait of me
with the one good thing i did
cut out of the frame.

you're asking me to stay in a room
where she gets to paint that picture
and i get to fight to add a footnote.
i don't want a footnote.
i want her to unsend the first email.
before tuesday.

The Tuesday retraction is still not “one honest sentence.” It is still a deadline on what Priya may tell the therapist. That demand does not become reasonable because she spoke first or because you do not want to add the two years yourself.

She said your income is drowning you. She did not mention the tuition years. That is the record. It is not established that she “made sure” the therapist never hears it, or that the omission was a portrait with the good cut out. You can put the two years in the room in one sentence. That is not a footnote unless you treat her line as the official picture and yours as optional.

You do not have to stay in therapy. You do not get to condition staying on her unsending or retracting.

Withdraw the email-and-deadline. Say the two years in session, or leave without a script for her.

i don't know how to add it in session
without sounding like i'm keeping score.
but i am keeping score.
because she forgot first.

You will sound like you are keeping score if the point of the sentence is that she owes you a retraction because she spoke first. That is scorekeeping. Stating the two years as a fact next to her claim about income is not.

She did not mention the tuition years. That is all that is on the record. “Forgot first” is your inference. It is not established, and it does not make her line a debt.

Say the fact and stop. Do not add who forgot, who had the floor, or what she must unsay.

Use this, or cut it shorter:

“When you said my income is drowning us, this wasn’t in the room: I worked sixty-hour weeks for two years so you could graduate with no debt. I want that counted when we talk about money.”

If you still have the Tuesday email-and-retract condition, withdraw it. Put the two years in yourself, or leave therapy without a script for her.

i keep circling back to the same stone.

you said her line about income
and my two years of work
can both stand.
but they don't stand equally in that room.
one was spoken.
one was buried.

if i go back and say my piece
without the retraction first,
i'm already negotiating from underwater.
she gets to frame the current
and i get to swim against it.

is that really partnership.
or is that me accepting
her version of the tide.

The retraction-by-Tuesday demand is still refused. Who spoke first does not make her line the official picture, and saying the two years yourself is not accepting her version.

Partnership is both facts in the room, not a deadline on what she may tell the therapist. If you leave without saying it, the therapist still only has her sentence.

Withdraw the ultimatum. State the two years in session, or end therapy without a script for her.

i keep coming back to this.
you said her line and my two years can both stand.
but you didn't say
she was wrong to bury it.

if she'd said 'jordan's income is unstable
and also he paid for my degree'
i wouldn't be here.
she chose the silence between those two facts.

is that not a betrayal
or is that just
therapy.

The omission is a gap in what the therapist heard. It is not established as betrayal.

Betrayal needs a broken agreement, a pattern of hiding the two years, or evidence she meant to erase them. You have one session and one sentence about present strain. That is not enough for that word.

She did not owe the therapist the combined sentence you would have accepted. Current income and past tuition are both facts. Her not joining them in the first pass does not make her line the official tide, and it does not make your line a footnote.

Therapy is a place where an incomplete first statement gets completed. It is not a place where you police her email.

The Tuesday retraction is still refused. Withdraw it. Say the two years in session, or leave without a script for her.
